campbell.title: Campbell City Council — August 18, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered routine business including approval of past meeting minutes and payment of bills, as well as accepting a donation from the Campbell Police Foundation to support K9 veterinary care and equipment. The Council also took up two labor agreements covering police officers and carpenters, an annual bond oversight report, and a merit pay increase for the City Clerk contract.
keyTopics: Acceptance of $41,911.62 in Campbell Police Foundation donations for K9 veterinary services and equipment
Ratification of a new labor agreement (2026-2028) with the Campbell Peace Officers Association
Ratification of a new labor agreement (2026-2028) with the North Coast States Carpenters Union
FY 2025 Annual Report from the Citizen's Bond Oversight Committee for Measure O
Designation of voting delegates for the League of California Cities Annual Conference

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — August 19, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council took up a routine set of budget, contract, and infrastructure items, including janitorial services, irrigation maintenance, a GIS consultant contract, and a new Bellgrove Park playground. The Council also considered a five-year law enforcement agreement with the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office and a high-profile appeal involving a proposed 25-lot residential subdivision on Pierce Road.
keyTopics: Appeal of the Planning Commission's decision to deny Design Review and a Tentative Map for a 25-lot subdivision on a 72.45-acre Pierce Road parcel
Five-year law enforcement services agreement with the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office
Contracts for the Bellgrove Park playground replacement project
No Parking Anytime zone proposed for Chester Avenue and Arcadia Palms Drive
Purchase of electric equipment to replace gas systems at Warner Hutton House, Civic Center Theater, and Joan Pisani Community Center

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — August 25, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council considered several construction and infrastructure items, including a roof replacement at the History Museum, EV chargers at the Maintenance Yard, and completion of the Woodland Library Patio Expansion. The Council also held a public hearing on a resident petition to rename Lee Street to Tubman Street, and reviewed vesting tentative maps for two condominium developments.
keyTopics: Public hearing on renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street, with options to approve or refer to the Historical Commission for further study
Vesting tentative maps for 19 condominium units at 349 First Street and 33 condominium units at Sherwood and Acacia Avenues
Contract award for History Museum roof replacement (not-to-exceed $147,500 plus contingency) and Maintenance Yard EV Chargers project (not-to-exceed $363,220)
Acceptance of completed Woodland Library Patio Expansion project
Draft responses to Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's oversight of BART Silicon Valley Phase II

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 18, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council considered a routine agenda covering financial reporting, staffing agreements, and municipal code updates. Items included a monthly financial report, approval of accounts payable and payroll records, appointment of a voting delegate for a statewide city association event, and a public hearing item related to an appeal.
keyTopics: Monthly Financial and Investment Report for June 2026
Accounts Payable Check Registers and Payroll Reports
Voting delegate and alternate appointment for the League of California Cities Annual event
Omnibus ordinance making minor updates to the Town Code
Public hearing appeal request and second amendment to a professional services agreement

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — August 26, 2026
san-jose.summary: This was a procedural Rules and Open Government Committee meeting focused on organizing upcoming City Council agendas rather than debating policy. The Committee reviewed the final agenda for the September 1, 2026 Council meeting and considered a VEBA Advisory Committee appointment, while the September 8 meeting was cancelled.
keyTopics: Review and finalization of the September 1, 2026 Council meeting agenda, including possible new items and time-certain scheduling
Cancellation of the September 8, 2026 draft agenda review
Public record covering August 13–20, 2026
VEBA Advisory Committee appointment
Joint special meeting planning with the San José/Santa Clara Treatment Plant Advisory Committee

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — August 25, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council held a regular session that began with public comments on topics not otherwise on the agenda. The Council then met in closed session to discuss performance evaluations for its two Council-appointed employees and to review labor negotiation matters concerning those same unrepresented positions.
keyTopics: Public comment period for items not on the agenda
Closed-session performance evaluation of the City Clerk and City Manager
Closed-session labor negotiations discussion involving the City Clerk and City Manager as unrepresented employees

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a special meeting on August 25, 2026, that began with a closed session for confidential discussion, followed by a public session featuring a presentation on the CleanWater Program. No regular legislative business was listed on this agenda.
keyTopics: Closed session
CleanWater Program update presentation

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — August 12, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino Teen Commission met to discuss plans for a Bike Fest event and a Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program. They also heard from a youth-led organization called Next Vision AI and approved minutes from a previous meeting.
keyTopics: Bike Fest event planning
Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program
Presentation from youth-led organization Next Vision AI
Approval of June 10, 2026 meeting minutes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting was held in a hybrid format, allowing one councilmember to participate remotely from India while others attended in person or via Zoom. The agenda excerpt provided is largely procedural, covering remote participation logistics and public comment submission instructions rather than substantive policy items.
keyTopics: Councilmember Chahal's remote participation from Panchkula, India
Hybrid meeting format with in-person and Zoom access options
Procedures for submitting written public comment before the meeting

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 11, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered introducing an ordinance amending part of the city's municipal code and received an educational presentation on how municipal bonds work. The meeting also included routine business such as the council calendar, meeting minutes, and lists of upcoming and requested agenda items.
keyTopics: Introduction of an ordinance amending Municipal Code Title XIII, Chapters B.6
Presentation on 'Municipal Bonds 101' from Finance staff
Review of the City Council calendar of meetings
Preview of anticipated items for the next regular Council meeting
Review of agenda items requested by Councilmembers

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Public Art Commission — August 20, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Public Art Commission reviewed a public art plan for the 3150 El Camino Real private development, with a presentation from the project's art consultant, artist, and developer. The Commission also considered funding for temporary interactive media art installations and the acceptance of donated artworks from two local artists.
keyTopics: Approval of June 18, 2026 meeting minutes
Final review of public art plan for the 3150 El Camino Real development, with presentation by artist Giles Miller and Acclaim Companies
Allocation of up to $70,000 for Code:ART 2027 temporary interactive media installations
Acceptance of donated artworks by CASP artists Adrienne Defendi and Eric Fei
